checks.description: OLS+HC3 recovers a planted slope of -0.5 within its own 95% CI
statsmodels beta equals an independent normal-equation OLS on the published scatter
25 random published country-year values equal the raw WDI value (after rounding) or both are null
assert_same_basis raises for PPP vs current-USD and PPP vs constant-USD
a second clustering run gives identical assignments
no aggregate code appears in any panel, ranking, regression point or cluster
every ranking contains exactly the countries with a value that year

agriculture+industry+services value-added shares sum to 70..110 percent in at least 97 percent of complete country-years, median 88..100 (value added is at basic prices, so the gap to 100 is net product taxes, not an error)
2019 PPP and constant-USD GDP per capita rank-correlate above 0.9 (different bases, same economies; sanity only, never compared as levels)

limitations_observed: Unconditional beta: poor-country growth depends on factors absent here; conditional convergence is not estimated.
Terciles and pop-weighted fits have wide CIs; early-window samples (1960) cover about half the countries and are not a random sample.
Cluster silhouette is low (weak separation); groups are descriptive and the k choice is rule-based, not a discovery of natural classes.
Value-added shares sum to about 93 percent of GDP at the median (net product taxes make up the rest); they are not a full decomposition of GDP.
hhi5 uses five broad export groups; product-level concentration is higher.
WDI revises history and later years are estimates; successor-state early values are reconstructions.
